translationRepairs: His father Yao Yi, courtesy name Shanyi, had served as commissioner of Yi Prefecture during the Zhenguan reign and was posthumously honored as Grand Military Commissioner of You Prefecture with the posthumous name Wenxian.

His father Yao Yi, courtesy name Shanyi, had served as commander-in-chief of Xi Prefecture during the Zhenguan reign and was posthumously honored as Grand Commander-in-chief of You Prefecture with the posthumous name Wenxian.

巂州 is Xi Prefecture, not Yi Prefecture, and 都督/大都督 are commander-in-chief titles, not commissioner. The proposed parenthesis with the Chinese toponym cannot stand in the English field, so the same correction is kept without the graph.

His father Yi, styled Shanyi, in the Zhenguan era served as military commissioner of Yi Prefecture, was posthumously made Grand Military Commissioner of You Prefecture, and given the posthumous title Wenxian.

His father Yi, styled Shanyi, in the Zhenguan era served as commander-in-chief of Xi Prefecture, was posthumously made Grand Commander-in-chief of You Prefecture, and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
The literal line repeats the same misreading of 巂州 as Yi and of 都督 as military commissioner.

I thought them wronged, yet feared that when close ministers interrogated them, all obtained their written confessions that they were not wronged; I had no doubts and at once approved their memorials.
I thought them wronged, but when close ministers went to interrogate them they all obtained written confessions that there was no injustice; I had no doubts and at once approved their memorials.
The original treats 畏 as Wu fearing the ministers; the clause reports that close ministers' interrogations produced written statements of no injustice, after which she approved.
In the third year of Shenglì he was promoted to associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
In the third year of Shengli he was promoted to joint manager of affairs with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace (chancellor).
同鳳閣鸞台平章事 is the Wu-Zhou chancellor formula tong pingzhangshi, not an associate directorship of the two departments; 平章事 is omitted in the original.

The crown prince was afraid and submitted a memorial accusing Chong and the others of driving a wedge into the royal house, asking that they be punished; they were demoted to Prefect of Shen Prefecture.

The crown prince was afraid and submitted a memorial accusing Chong and the others of driving a wedge into the royal house, asking that they be punished; Chong was demoted to Prefect of Shen Prefecture.
貶為申州刺史 is grammatically singular and the following transfers (徐、潞、揚州) continue Yao Chong alone, so 'they were demoted' is a subject error.
Empress Wu built the Xian Temple at vast expense, and the Retired Emperor built the Jinxian and Yuzhen abbeys, costing millions;
Empress Wu built Fuxian Temple at vast expense, and the Retired Emperor built the Jinxian and Yuzhen abbeys, costing millions;
福先寺 is the temple name Fuxian; 'Xian Temple' drops 福.
Empress Wu built blessings at Xian Temple; the Retired Emperor built the two abbeys Jinxian and Yuzhen, costing millions;
Empress Wu built Fuxian Temple; the Retired Emperor built the two abbeys Jinxian and Yuzhen, costing millions;
造福先寺 is building Fuxian Temple, not 'building blessings at Xian Temple'.
In Zhongzong's time, close kin memorialized to ordain monks and nuns; warm households and strong young men thereby avoided rent and corvée.
In Zhongzong's time, close kin memorialized to ordain monks and nuns; affluent households and strong young men thereby avoided rent and corvée.
溫戶 are well-off registered households, not thermally warm households.
In time Zhao Hui, an assistant in the Bureau of Astronomy, was found to have taken bribes from foreigners and faced execution.
In time Zhao Hui, a clerk of the Purple Forbidden Secretariat, was found to have taken bribes from foreigners and faced execution.
紫微史 is a clerk of the Purple Forbidden (Zhongshu) Secretariat under Xuanzong, not a Bureau of Astronomy post; 紫微令 in the same chapter names that secretariat.
After a long while, Assistant in the Bureau of Astronomy Zhao Hui received bribes from barbarians and should die.
After a long while, Zhao Hui, a clerk of the Purple Forbidden Secretariat, received bribes from barbarians and should die.
The literal line makes the same astronomy error for 紫微史.
Fearing for himself, Chong resigned the chancellorship, recommended Song Jing as successor, and was relieved of office with the honorific rank of Defender-in-Chief.
Fearing for himself, Chong resigned the chancellorship, recommended Song Jing as successor, and was relieved of government affairs with the honorific rank of Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes.
開府儀同三司 is the prestige rank Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes; 罷政事 is relief from government affairs, not appointment as Defender-in-Chief (太尉).

Chong was fearful; he returned the chancellorship, brought in Song Jing to replace him, and was dismissed from government affairs with the title of Defender-in-Chief and Concurrent Supervisor of State Affairs.
Chong was fearful; he returned the chancellorship, brought in Song Jing to replace him, and was dismissed from government affairs with the title Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes.
The original invents Defender-in-Chief and Concurrent Supervisor of State Affairs; the Chinese only grants 開府儀同三司 on dismissal from 政事.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as Defender-in-Chief of Yangzhou with the posthumous name Wenxian.
He was posthumously made Grand Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
贈揚州大都督 is a posthumous grand area-command title, not enfeoffment as Defender-in-Chief.
He was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief of Yangzhou; his posthumous title was Wenxian (Literary and Illustrious).
He was posthumously made Grand Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou; his posthumous title was Wenxian (Literary and Illustrious).
The literal line likewise renders 大都督 as Defender-in-Chief.
More recently Emperor Xiahe sent agents to buy the release of animals; Princess Taiping, Wu Sansi, and others ordained followers and built temples—yet they were executed and became a laughingstock.
More recently Emperor Xiaohe sent agents to buy the release of animals; Princess Taiping, Wu Sansi, and others ordained followers and built temples—yet they were executed and became a laughingstock.
孝和 is Xiaohe (Zhongzong's posthumous designation); Xiahe is a wrong romanization.
He had three sons—Yi, Yi, and Yi—each rising to ministerial rank or provincial governorship.
He had three sons—Yi (Yí), Yi (Yì, 'different'), and Yi (Yì, 'chess')—each rising to ministerial rank or provincial governorship.

The three given names 彝、異、弈 are distinct and must not be collapsed to identical unmarked Yi; the proposed character glosses cannot stand in the English field, so tone marks and brief English senses disambiguate them.
Yi asked to administer Ju, became prefect of Suiyang, then was recalled and made Grand Master of the Herds.
Yi asked to take on a demanding jurisdiction, became prefect of Suiyang, then was recalled and made Grand Master of the Herds.
請治劇 is a request for a demanding jurisdiction, not a toponym Ju.
He requested to govern Ju, served as prefect of Suiyang, and was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Herds.
He requested to govern a demanding commandery, served as prefect of Suiyang, and was summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Herds.
劇 names a class of difficult post, not a place Ju; 睢陽 is the prefecture that follows.
While prefect of Tongzhou, he incurred Zhang Shuo's lasting enmity; Shuo induced Zhao Yanzhao to impeach him.
While prefect of Tongzhou, he incurred Zhang Yue's lasting enmity; Yue induced Zhao Yanzhao to impeach him.
張說 here is the statesman conventionally Zhang Yue; reading 說 as Shuo splits the same person from later Yue.
Promoted to Left Bureau Censor-in-Chief, he learned that Zhang Changzong had consulted a fortune-teller; he demanded a full inquiry. The Empress replied, "Yizhi has already told me himself."

Promoted to Left Bureau Censor-in-Chief, he learned that Zhang Changzong had consulted a fortune-teller; he demanded a full inquiry. The Empress replied, "Yizhi and the others have already told me themselves."
易之等 is plural; dropping 等 makes the empress's quotation a singular confession by Yizhi alone.
Her mood softened, and she allowed Yizhi and his brother to be jailed.
Her mood softened, and she allowed Yizhi and the others to be jailed.
許收易之等就獄 is 'Yizhi and the others'; 'his brother' over-specifies 等.
Yizhi had hoped to destroy Jing once he left the capital; foiled, he planned to murder him at his son's wedding.
Yizhi had hoped to destroy Jing once he left the capital; foiled, he planned to murder him at a wedding in Jing's household.
家婚禮 is a wedding in Jing's household; the original invents a son not named in this sentence.
Jing rebuked him: "The crown prince rules openly—the prince of Tang should return to his fief; why meddle in government? Have you forgotten Lü Lu?"

Jing rebuked him: "Rightful sovereign rule has now been restored—the prince should retire to his marquisate; how can he still meddle in court affairs? Have you not seen the affair of Lü Chan and Lü Lu?"
復子明辟 is restoration of rightful sovereign rule, not the crown prince ruling openly; 王 addresses Wu Sansi, not a prince of Tang; 產、祿 are Lü Chan and Lü Lu.
In the Zhenguan era, when the Princess of Changle was married, Wei Zheng said one must not add to the Princess of Changle; Taizong gladly accepted, and Empress Wende sent envoys with generous thanks.

In the Zhenguan era, when the Princess of Changle was married, Wei Zheng said one must not add honors as for a Grand Princess; Taizong gladly accepted, and Empress Wende sent envoys with generous thanks.
不可加長公主 contrasts 長樂公主 with the higher rank 長公主 (Grand Princess), not a second mention of Princess Changle.
If Your Majesty cannot sway the empress, permit at least a first-rank consort's tomb by the mausoleum—four zhang high, which is near the proper measure."
If the empress's feeling cannot be overborne, I request approving the statute for a first-rank accompanying burial at the imperial tomb, a mound four zhang—roughly fitting what is proper."
中宮情不可奪 is the empress's feeling, not 'Your Majesty'; 一品陪陵 is the first-rank accompanying-mausoleum statute, not a consort's or attendant's tomb. The proposal fixes the agent but still misrenders 陪陵.
To punish lenders for knowing would imply they should have refused—and that would brand refusal as aiding the rebel.
If they had known and still refused to lend, that would have been to side with rebellion.
使知而不假，是與為反 is a counterfactual: knowing the plot and refusing to lend would have been siding with rebellion.

After the Shengli era Moqi chou of the Turks, counting on strength, raided the frontier and attacked the Bayegu of the Nine Surnames; emboldened by victory he rode out carelessly, was ambushed and killed, and frontier envoy Hao Lingjian brought his head to the capital.

After the Shengli era Mo Chuo of the Türks, counting on strength, raided the frontier and attacked the Bayegu of the Nine Surnames; emboldened by victory he rode out carelessly, was ambushed and killed, and the envoy to the frontier Hao Lingquan brought his head to the capital.
默啜 is Mo Chuo, not Moqi chou. The unit's 郝靈亻 is a broken 郝靈佺: Wikisource juan 124 has the same truncated graph, immediately completed as 靈佺, and the parallel Xin Tangshu account writes 郝靈佺 in full.
His son Sheng rose to Vice Minister of the Stud.
His son Sheng was Vice Minister of the Stud.
子升，升，太僕少卿 restates the name 升 then the office; treating the second 升 as the verb 'rose' is an extraction artifact.
His son Hun, close to Li Linfu, served as Remonstrating Censor, Administrator of Pingyuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Eastern Capital commissioner.
His son Hun, close to Li Linfu, successively served as Grand Master of Remonstrance, Administrator of Pingyuan, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Eastern Capital Investigating Commissioner.
諫議大夫 is Grand Master of Remonstrance, not Remonstrating Censor; 東京採訪使 is Eastern Capital Investigating Commissioner; 曆/歷 marks successive tenure.

unresolvedReferences.description: 二張 / the two Zhang brothers: Zhang Yizhi is named; the second Zhang is not named in this chunk.
五王 / the Five Princes are a named collective; individuals are not listed here.
Zhang Jingzang's counsel is dated only to Yao Chong's twentieth year, which the chapter does not convert to a Western year.
Zhao Ming's historical identity is not established in the chapter.
Chong's two sons in Luoyang are not named and are not mapped onto 彝/異/弈.
Which son's line produced great-grandsons He and Xu is not stated.
房 and 杜 are surnames only; conventionally Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui, not named in full in this chapter.
郝靈亻 is a damaged form of 郝靈佺; English Hao Lingjian vs Lingqian is the same envoy.
